note: Canonical security class table. Each class is an application-level weakness that web and code scanners commonly report and require fixing, mapped to OWASP Top 10:2021 and CWE. The table is project-neutral: patterns name APIs and value shapes, never a product route, host or field from one application. golden names the Golden rule that states the same obligation; when it is null, agrimap-agent-skills has no direct rule and the class is a package security baseline (tier SHOULD, sourceStatusBasis external-security-standard), never a Golden verdict. Every class is a lexical review candidate: reachability, caller identity and compensating controls (gateway, shared middleware, global policy) are not provable from text. responseContract is the fix boundary carried into prompts: a legitimate, authorized request must keep its status, body and wire names; only malicious, malformed or unauthorized requests may change outcome.

classes.title: SQL text assembled from values
classes.observation: Pass values as command or stored-procedure parameters; keep SQL text constant and quote identifiers through an allow-list or QUOTENAME.
classes.responseContract: Parameterization changes how values travel, not which rows a legitimate value selects. Do not reject or strip quotes, semicolons or dashes from input: valid names and text contain them.

classes.title: Command, script or type name taken from a non-literal value
classes.observation: Map caller input to a fixed allow-list of commands, scripts or types; pass process arguments as an argument list, never as one composed string.
classes.responseContract: Every currently valid choice stays reachable through the allow-list with the same result; only values outside the list are refused.

classes.title: LDAP filter assembled from values
classes.observation: Escape each value with an RFC 4515 filter encoder before it enters the filter; keep the filter structure constant.
classes.responseContract: Encoding preserves the meaning of legitimate names (including parentheses, asterisks and non-ASCII text), so the same directory entries are returned.

classes.title: File path built from a caller-shaped name without containment
classes.observation: Resolve the full path and require it to stay under the approved root, or map an identifier to a stored path; Path.GetFileName alone does not cover every caller.
classes.responseContract: Files inside the approved root keep the same content, name and content type; only paths that escape the root are refused (404 or 400 per the existing error contract).

classes.title: Endpoint reachable without an authorization requirement
classes.observation: Apply the standard class-level [Authorize] (or a fallback policy) and keep explicit anonymous access for endpoints that are public by design; remove test, mock and bypass endpoints from deployable code.
classes.responseContract: Authenticated callers with the needed role keep the same response. Anonymous access stays only on endpoints that are public by design (login, token refresh, health, public lookup); confirm each before adding a requirement.

classes.title: Exception or diagnostic detail sent to the caller
classes.observation: Log the exception with a correlation id and return the established error code and a stable user message; keep developer exception pages and detailed errors behind the development environment.
classes.responseContract: Keep the HTTP status, error code and response shape; only the internal text (exception message, stack trace, SQL or type names) leaves the message field.

classes.title: Credential or personal value written to a log
classes.owasp: A09:2021 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
classes.observation: Log an identifier, a masked form or a presence flag instead of the value; keep EnableSensitiveDataLogging behind the development environment.
classes.responseContract: Logging changes never touch the response. Keep the event, level and correlation fields so operations and audit queries still work.

classes.title: Weak hash, cipher, key size or random source
classes.observation: Use SHA-256 or stronger, AES-GCM, RSA 2048+ or ECDSA P-256, signing keys of at least 256 bits and RandomNumberGenerator for secrets; a non-security checksum may keep its algorithm when documented.
classes.responseContract: Stored hashes, tokens and encrypted values issued before the change must stay verifiable: verify old and new forms during migration and re-hash on next successful use.

classes.title: Token validation switched off or bypassed
classes.observation: Validate issuer, audience, lifetime and signing key with signed tokens required; decode-only reads must never decide access.
classes.responseContract: Tokens issued by the real issuer for this audience keep working; set the valid issuer and audience lists from every issuer currently in use before enabling each check.

classes.title: Token issued without expiry or unique id
classes.observation: Issue tokens with exp and a unique jti (UUID) so expiry and replay checks are possible; sign HS256 with a key of at least 256 bits or use RS256/ES256.
classes.responseContract: Add claims without removing or renaming existing ones, and keep the current lifetime unless the owner changes it, so consumers that read the token keep working.

classes.title: TLS certificate validation disabled or weak protocol pinned
classes.observation: Use default certificate validation and trust an internal CA through the platform trust store instead of a callback that accepts any certificate; leave protocol selection to the OS (TLS 1.2+).
classes.responseContract: Calls to hosts with valid certificates are unchanged; install the internal CA before removing the bypass so legitimate internal calls keep succeeding.

classes.title: Deserializer that can instantiate caller-chosen types
classes.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures
classes.observation: Use System.Text.Json or a serializer bound to known contract types; avoid BinaryFormatter-family serializers and TypeNameHandling other than None.
classes.responseContract: Payloads that match the declared contract types deserialize to the same values; only type-directed payloads are refused.

classes.title: CORS policy accepts any origin
classes.observation: List the application origins from configuration; never combine any-origin with credentials.
classes.responseContract: Every origin that calls the API today stays on the list, taken from configuration per environment, so browser callers keep working.

classes.title: HTTP method override accepted
classes.observation: Route each operation by its real HTTP method and stop honoring X-HTTP-Method-Override or _method.
classes.responseContract: Requests sent with their real method are unchanged; confirm no client relies on the override before removing it.

classes.title: Redirect target taken from a non-literal value
classes.observation: Redirect only to local paths (LocalRedirect, Url.IsLocalUrl) or to an allow-listed host; in the browser, route in-app with the router.
classes.responseContract: Local and allow-listed targets redirect exactly as before; only foreign targets fall back to the default page.

classes.title: Credential or personal value carried in the URL query
classes.observation: Send credentials and personal identifiers in the body or a header; renaming the query field does not remove the exposure.
classes.responseContract: Moving a value out of the query changes the API contract: add the body or header form first, keep the old form during an agreed migration and remove it only after every consumer moves.

classes.title: Secret or personal field in a response contract
classes.observation: Never return secrets, password hashes or salts; return personal fields only to a caller authorized for that record and only in the projections that need them.
classes.responseContract: Do not mask or encrypt a personal field for every caller: an authorized owner or officer who legitimately reads it must keep the same value. Fix authorization and projection scope, and confirm each consumer before removing a field.

classes.title: Paging or size input without bounds
classes.observation: Declare a [Range] (or equivalent validation) on paging and size values, using an integer type for row counts and offsets.
classes.responseContract: Choose the upper bound from the largest legitimate use (exports, 'all' views) so valid requests keep the same result; only out-of-range values get the existing validation error. Do not clamp silently.

classes.title: Host pipeline without visible transport and response headers
classes.observation: Confirm where HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Cache-Control for sensitive responses are set (application, shared middleware or gateway) and set them in one owner.
classes.responseContract: Headers do not change the body. Send Cache-Control: no-store only for authenticated or personal responses and keep caching for public assets such as map tiles; enable HSTS only on HTTPS origins and grow max-age gradually. Public-Key-Pins (HPKP) is deprecated and is not recommended.

classes.title: Cookie without Secure, HttpOnly or a safe SameSite
classes.observation: Set Secure and HttpOnly on session and auth cookies and SameSite=Lax or Strict unless a cross-site flow needs None with Secure.
classes.responseContract: Keep cookie names, paths and lifetimes; confirm no script reads a cookie before making it HttpOnly and that the site is HTTPS end to end before requiring Secure.

classes.title: HTML or script sink that bypasses Angular sanitization
classes.observation: Bind text through interpolation, let Angular sanitize [innerHTML], and keep bypassSecurityTrust* for constant or server-sanitized content only.
classes.responseContract: Output encoding changes how text is rendered, not what data the API returns; formatted content that must stay HTML is sanitized, not dropped.

classes.title: Auth token or credential kept in Web Storage
classes.observation: Prefer an HttpOnly, Secure cookie or in-memory storage with a short-lived refresh flow; never store passwords.
classes.responseContract: Changing token storage changes the auth flow across frontend, backend and gateway: migrate in stages and keep existing sessions valid until they expire.
